assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: labeled modular spaceship KIT SHEET for a mobile cyberpunk space-survival builder.
Follow the user's brief closely:
Modular spaceship kit sheet, orthographic views (front, side, top), clean light-grey background, parts laid out on a grid like a game asset sheet.
Style: future cyberpunk space survival, hard-surface sci-fi, dark gunmetal hull with neon cyan accent lights, worn industrial panels, bold readable silhouettes.
Modules: cockpit, 2x2 hull block, 2x4 hull block, corridor, cargo bay, engine (large/small), thruster, turret, reactor core, solar panel, docking port.
Each module has standardized square connection ports on its faces, marked with glowing yellow-black edge frames, all modules snap on a 2m grid.
Color coding: reactor=cyan, weapons=orange-red, living=warm white.
Mobile game asset style, low-poly friendly, simple large shapes, no tiny greebles, labeled parts, concept art, high detail, 8k
Composition clarification: one very high-resolution LANDSCAPE reference atlas, a disciplined FOUR-COLUMN by THREE-ROW grid, twelve module cells total. Each cell contains THREE small clean orthographic projections of the SAME component: front, side and top. Keep each component simple enough that its three views remain readable. Do not turn it into twelve whole spaceships. All silhouettes fully visible, clear spacing, no cropping, neutral consistent illumination. Aim for the maximum available native resolution and 8K-level detail in the concept, while retaining large low-poly-friendly shapes.
The twelve cells, in reading order, must have exactly these legible labels:
"COCKPIT"; "HULL 2x2"; "HULL 2x4"; "CORRIDOR";
"CARGO BAY"; "ENGINE L"; "ENGINE S"; "THRUSTER";
"TURRET"; "REACTOR"; "SOLAR PANEL"; "DOCKING PORT".
A small shared legend may contain exactly "FRONT / SIDE / TOP" and "GRID 2m".
Design language: practical angular dark gunmetal modules, large beveled plates and readable panel breaks, restrained edge abrasion and industrial wear, precise inset cyan lights, bright yellow rim pieces interrupted by BLACK hazard stripes around square connection interfaces. Hazard strips must be visible in the light-gray sheet. Warm-white light in cockpit/living/corridor sections, cyan reactor accents, orange-red weapon accents.
All modules expose compatible SQUARE attachment faces; do not use circular docking collars as the standard interface. Engine nozzles can be round or faceted but their attachment faces are square. Docking port is a square framed unit. Hull 2x4 has twice the planar length of Hull 2x2 at the SAME width and comparable height. Interpret 2x2 and 2x4 as grid footprints on a 2m snap lattice, not as a guarantee that a person's room is only 2m tall. Personnel clearance and final engineered wall thickness remain a later modeling constraint. The solar panel includes its foldable panel surface and square-root mount as one component.
Keep the requested industrial cyberpunk finish, not clean white luxury ceramic. Do not introduce extra colors, neon-covered surfaces, tiny greebles, fantasy ornament, logos, an assembled hero ship, a city, a starfield, UI widgets or upgrade arrows. This is a concept asset atlas; labels and geometry clarity take priority over decorative graphics.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: modular spaceship assembly comparison board for a mobile cyberpunk space-survival builder.
Input image 1: REFERENCE ONLY — the authoritative module kit atlas. Use its module designs, materials, lights and square interface proportions consistently; do not reproduce the atlas grid.
Primary request: Three spaceships assembled from the same modular kit: small scout (6 modules), medium cargo hauler (20 modules), large battle station (50+ modules). Visible module seams and connection ports so the assembly logic is clear. Same art style as the kit sheet, side-by-side comparison, dark space background, orthographic 3/4 view.
Composition: one landscape comparison image, exactly three distinct assembled vessels arranged horizontally from small to large, separated with breathing room. All three use the same orthographic three-quarter camera angle and comparable module scale, so the larger structures really contain more modules instead of merely enlarging the same hull. Every vessel is fully visible. Near-black space with restrained stars, no planet or distracting scenery.
Left: compact SMALL SCOUT, a short forward cockpit and slim body with two small rear engines, six main modules clearly bounded by seams. Center: MEDIUM CARGO HAULER, elongated central spine with paired cargo pods attached along the sides and two large rear engines, twenty main modules. Right: LARGE BATTLE STATION, a broad cross-shaped or branched platform assembled from fifty-plus repeated modules, with docks, cargo pods, reactor sections, solar panels and orange-red turret clusters. It must read as a constructed station, not a giant smooth battlecruiser.
The purpose is to show player creativity using ONE kit: scout is narrow, hauler has a long spine and wide cargo racks, station has a branching architecture. Reuse recognizable parts from the input atlas at compatible interfaces. Never fuse all parts into a monolithic hull.
Clearly visible physical panel boundaries, attachment joints and unused square ports, with yellow-and-black interface rims. Connected modules meet flush, with no floating disconnected parts or impossible interpenetration. Count targets apply to main assembled blocks, not little armor panels or exhaust details.
Materials: dark gunmetal, worn industrial hard-surface panels, controlled cyan light strips, warm-white living/cockpit windows, orange-red weapons. Keep the atlas's bold readable mobile-game silhouettes and large low-poly-friendly forms. Render with polished PBR-like metal and restrained edge wear, no dense tiny greebles. Subtle neutral rim light keeps all module seams readable against dark space.
Typography: simple and unobtrusive, exactly these three captions beneath the respective craft:
"SMALL SCOUT · 6 MODULES"
"CARGO HAULER · 20 MODULES"
"BATTLE STATION · 50+ MODULES"
No other text, no logos, no arrows, no UI, no bright colored background. High-quality concept art; maximum available native resolution.

steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: in-game screenshot CONCEPT for a mobile cyberpunk sci-fi survival builder, landscape screen.
Input image 1: REFERENCE ONLY — the authoritative module kit atlas. The player's ship must visibly be assembled from those same dark gunmetal modules, square yellow-black attachment rims, cyan inset light strips and warm-white cockpit windows.
Primary request: In-game screenshot concept, mobile sci-fi survival builder, player-built modular ship floating near a derelict station, 3/4 top-down camera, neon cyan and magenta lighting, visible build grid hologram, UI-friendly composition with empty space at screen edges, cinematic but readable.
Composition: a single cinematic but highly readable landscape game-view image. Orthographic-like three-quarter TOP-DOWN camera showing the upper surfaces and sides, suitable for playing a mobile ship-building game. A compact-to-medium player-built modular ship sits near the central lower-left area and a larger derelict modular station occupies the upper-right middle distance. Both remain inside a central safe content zone; leave generous uncluttered dark space at all screen edges for future touch controls and resource UI. No painted HUD, no text, no logos.
Player ship: recognizably kit-built, with forward cockpit, a central hull spine, exposed seams, several offset cargo/utility modules, a cyan reactor and twin engines. Allow a practical slightly asymmetric builder layout with a spare square port. The ship remains the primary subject, clearly readable at phone size.
A localized cyan holographic square build grid aligns with the player's ship, on a consistent 2m snap lattice. Add one simple translucent preview hull module beside an empty compatible attachment face to communicate building. Grid is restrained and stops around the ship; it does not cover the entire screen or obscure the hull. The ghost is visibly a placement preview and the assembled ship has real connected geometry.
Derelict station: damaged modular architecture with readable broken hull sections and docking structures, some faded cyan lighting and magenta environmental spill. A small amount of nearby debris provides abandoned-space mood without visual clutter.
Lighting: neon cyan from functional ship systems, magenta rim/environment light from the derelict station, dark neutral space, controlled bloom. Preserve local contrast on the gunmetal panels, yellow-black square interfaces and warm-white living sections. High-end game art materials and cinematic light, but simple broad shapes and visible construction logic remain paramount.
Avoid giant white luxury hulls, seamless organic ships, heavy fog, excessive bloom, dense tiny greebles, explosions, many ships, fake UI, giant typography, or photorealistic cockpit interiors. Render as a polished visual target, not a claim of an actual running game. Maximum available native resolution.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the referenced gameplay atmosphere concept. Change ONLY camera framing and placement to create better mobile UI safe margins.
Keep the exact same gunmetal cyberpunk module designs, square yellow-black ports, cyan and magenta light, warm-white cockpit, worn panels, derelict station identity, build grid and translucent module preview. Keep the same three-quarter top-down orthographic-like game camera.
Pull the camera back about 25–30%. Fit BOTH the complete player ship with its entire build grid AND the complete visible derelict station structure inside the central area of the canvas. Move the station down and left enough that no station structure, antenna or light is cut off at the top or right borders.
Leave a continuous band of calm, uncluttered dark space around ALL FOUR image edges, about 10–12% of the image dimension, suitable for mobile controls and HUD. The station can occupy the upper-right central area and the ship the lower-left central area. The player ship stays the primary subject and retains clear readable individual modules at mobile scale.
Do not change the asset art style, add new objects, add HUD/text, remove the holographic grid, or redesign the ship. Preserve the wide landscape aspect ratio and polished game concept quality.
